pr_title: analyze: also find template unit when an instance is specified
pr_body:
Fixes a regression caused by 2f6181ad4d6c126e3ebf6880ba30b3b0059c6fc8.

Fixes #30357.

### Unexpected behaviour you saw

https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/30172#issuecomment-1844699620
> This PR triggers a failure in Git's test suite (which has some support for setting up repository maintenance via systemd). It has unit files for several timers (`git-maintenance@hourly.timer`, `git-maintenance@daily.timer`, etc) along with a template service file (`git-maintenance@.service`) and expects to be able to verify per-timer services (e.g. `git-maintenance@hourly.service`) even though no specific unit file exists.
> 
> As a more minimal example, this used to work:
> 
> ```shell
> cat >foo@.service <<-\EOF
> [Service]
> ExecStart=ls
> EOF
> systemd-analyze verify foo@bar.service
> ```
> 
> and would use the `foo@.service` file. But as of [2f6181a](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/commit/2f6181ad4d6c126e3ebf6880ba30b3b0059c6fc8), it yields:
> 
> ```
> Unit foo@bar.service not found.
> ```
> 
> presumably because we break out of `verify_set_unit_path()` after seeing that the literal unit filename does not exist (and then whatever code later resolved the template name does not see that unit path at all).
